title: Stitching mismatched prefix IDs causing duplicated spikes in per-model charts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Console shows recurring narrow spike rows for certain customers in per-model daily charts immediately after backfill windows. Spikes correlate with late streaming events and subsequent batch backfills. This ticket investigates root cause and implements a durable deduplication strategy at the ingestion layer so console charts and per-model breakdowns reflect correct token/req counts.
reproduction_steps: Identify a customer with narrow spike rows in model X on 2026-02-14 to 2026-02-17
Query raw ingest events (streaming shard events + batch backfill events) for that customer and model over the window
Observe overlapping events with different prefix_id fields but identical logical request fingerprints (customer_id, request_id, model_alias, start_token_index)
Reconstruct per-token attribution used by the console and compare naive sum vs. deduplicated sum
investigation_notes: Initial telemetry shows duplicated rows originate from mismatched prefix_id assignment between streaming-bridge (real-time path) and backfill-job (batch path)
Streaming path uses request_prefix_id generated by front-end proxy; batch backfill regenerates prefix_id based on sampled request metadata which sometimes used a different hash salt (v1 vs v2)
Shard-merge logic assumed prefix_id stable across paths and used it as the primary dedupe key when aggregating, which fails when prefix IDs diverge
Affected customers have frequent short lived requests (avg length < 16 tokens) and our batching heuristics lead to identical logical requests being split across microbatches
Observed 1.8x overcount in token attribution for affected model/day windows in worst case
root_cause: Non-deterministic prefix_id generation across streaming and batch backfill (different hash salt/version)
Aggregation pipeline deduped solely on prefix_id and shard_merge metadata, which allowed collisions when prefix_id drifted
Late events were re-ingested without a stable global fingerprint and were merged into per-model timeseries as distinct samples
mitigation_plan: Hotfix: add secondary deterministic fingerprint at ingest that is computed from (customer_id, canonical_request_id, model_alias, input_hash) and store as event_fingerprint
Update aggregation to dedupe on event_fingerprint first, then prefix_id as fallback
Backfill: run a retroactive dedupe pass for the last 14 days for customers with < 10% variance alerts
Console UX: annotate affected chart windows with a 'backfill reconciliation' marker to avoid user confusion while retroactive job runs
acceptance_criteria: Per-model daily token totals for test dataset align within 1% of ground truth after dedupe
No new duplicate spikes appear for a controlled test customer over 7 days of simulated late events
E2E tests added to ingestion pipeline validating stable fingerprint across streaming and batch paths
Retroactive dedupe job completes for targeted customers and dashboards reflect corrected numbers
plan_timeline: 2026-02-18: Issue created after support ticket from customer-team
2026-02-20: Hotfix branch merged to ingestion (add event_fingerprint), deployed to staging
2026-02-24: Aggregation change merged to use fingerprint-first dedupe, deployed to canary
2026-02-27: Canary metrics looked good — reduced duplicate spikes on canary customers
2026-03-01: Retroactive dedupe job started for 7 high-variance customers
2026-03-02: Ticket moved to In Progress for expanded rollout and follow-ups
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/aggregator/pull/904 - prefer fingerprint dedupe and fallback to prefix_id
dashboards_and_alerts: pagerduty:/services/usage-analytics - on-call alerted for >10% day-over-day variance post-backfill
follow_ups: Add a short-lived audit log that records original prefix_id and computed event_fingerprint for every backfill event
Update documentation for backfill-job to specify hash salt/versioning policy and add compatibility tests
Investigate whether rate-limit retry flows are contributing to duplicate logical requests and add telemetry if so
final_resolution: Ongoing: hotfix reduced duplication on canary, retroactive dedupe corrected affected customers in first batch. Need to complete full 14-day dedupe and add cross-path CI tests before closing.
notes: PM Sofia Chen approved marking affected dashboards during rollout to reduce customer confusion
SRE Arjun Rao provided guidance on running the retro dedupe job with rate-limited write throughput to avoid downstream spikes
Customer success alerted three customers proactively and provided interim reconciled CSV exports
